data.title: Uniswap eyes $7.50, but crowded longs raise UNI’s risk
data.description:
Uniswap [UNI] moved toward $7.50 after briefly retracing from its supply-zone breakout. Retail activity rose alongside Spot buying, giving the recovery broader market participation.

Could this demand help UNI clear $7.50, or has bullish positioning made the rally more fragile?

Are UNI buyers gaining control?

UNI’s Open Interest climbed to $501 million over the last 24 hours. The increase suggested that derivatives traders added exposure as UNI approached the resistance level.

More strikingly, long positions represented 60% of market positioning, giving bulls an advantage in the derivatives market. However, this heavy long bias could increase liquidation risks if UNI’s momentum weakens.

But that is not the case now. Uniswap retail orders have also picked up, adding another layer of demand behind the recovery. The increasing buyer dominance on the spot market buying could give the rally more support and reduce its reliance on leveraged positions.

Can UNI reclaim $7.50?

On the daily chart, $7.50 remained the next major target for UNI bulls. The token traded above its key Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs), while bullish pressure continued building.

Notably, the price level anchors a huge liquidity cluster worth over $376 million, making it a significant target for the market players. Should the buyers keep absorbing the offer and UNI breaks above $7.50 with decent spot volume, the breakout may gather even more momentum when the liquidity around the level gets involved.

For UNI holders, it is also worth noting the bearish risks associated with the increased long position exposure at the moment. A breakdown from $7.50 might result in a number of leveraged liquidations and send UNI towards the nearest levels of support.

All in all, while taking into account the recent positive sentiment, the token’s technical outlook still looks promising. The network’s rising open interest, long positions dominance and increase buyers dominance on the spot market, all aligns with the token’s bullish bias.

Final Summary

  • UNI approached the crucial $7.50 resistance as Open Interest reached $501 million.
  • Long positions held a 60% share, supporting bulls while increasing liquidation risks.

data.title: Ethereum crypto price tests $2,434 support as sellers return
data.description:
The Ethereum crypto price fell 2.7% to $2,446 on Tuesday, September 15, extending its retreat from the $2,500 area.

The price of ETH briefly moved below the support at $2,434, but the buyers quickly bounced back. This movement left it prone to further fall if the said support level is breached.

Ethereum gives back its latest advance

Ethereum started trading at $2,515, reaching $2,519 before selling pushed the price to $2,431 for the day.

This sharp drop occurred after an earlier move saw it go down by 1.07% to $2,492.

The fall it saw after that shows that sellers remained active as trading continued. Volume reached 81,970 ETH, even though trading did not see the same levels seen during the rally in August.

Investors also exercised caution ahead of Tuesday’s crucial US Senate vote that might decide the advancement of the CLARITY Act. If it gathers sufficient endorsements from senators, lawmakers will start debating the Act.

Bitcoin also declined ahead of the vote, which means that the decline Ethereum is seeing was part of a broader caution across the crypto market.

Has the $2,434 support held?

The price fall to the $2,431 area took it below the level that traders are watching, but its recovery to $2,446 means buyers prevented a deeper fall during the session.

A brief move below support does not necessarily mean the price has broken down, and where it closes shows whether buyers have successfully defended the area.

The chart’s momentum reading stood at 54, indicating that $ETH was not at any particular extreme within its trading range and therefore perhaps less likely to undergo a short-term rebound.

Ethereum, however, still trades above its long-term moving averages, so despite the recent decline, the bigger recovery from the June lows is still intact.

If the price closes below $2,434 and selling continues, the next area to watch is around $2,385, but a recovery above $2,500 would ease the immediate pressure. If it is able to move beyond around $2,520, it would show that buyers have taken back control.

Final Summary

  • ETH was down 2.7%, trading briefly below the key support of $2,434.
  • A close below that could shift focus to $2,385, while $2,500 remains the first recovery hurdle.

data.title: PONS jumps 13%, hits $105M in volume – THESE levels define its breakout
data.description:
Pons [PONS] gained 13% in 24 hours, trading above $0.62. Trading volume also crossed $105 million. The rebound followed PONS’ reaction from the support zone of a bullish continuation pattern.

Such patterns emerge after a strong rally enters a consolidation phase before potentially resuming its previous direction.

During the early hours of the 14th of September, PONS rebounded from the pattern’s lower support. It then approached the descending resistance line and the critical horizontal level near $0.64.

Can PONS break above $0.64?

PONS’ recent pullback did not invalidate the bullish setup.

A confirmed break above resistance could push the token toward $0.97. Sustained momentum may then bring $1 within reach.

However, rejection from this level could extend the consolidation. PONS may consequently retreat toward the pattern’s lower boundary. The indicators presented a similarly divided picture.

The Accumulation/Distribution (A/D) indicator had risen since the 13th of September, reflecting stronger short-term buying pressure.

Even so, the A/D remained negative at -12.49 million. Sellers therefore retained broader control despite the recent recovery.

Meanwhile, the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) strengthened. The blue MACD line crossed above the orange signal line and moved toward positive territory.

A positive crossover could reinforce the breakout case. Until then, the indicator reflects improving momentum rather than complete bullish control.

Are spot buyers accumulating PONS?

Spot Market Netflow reached -$931,000 over 24 hours, while spot purchases totaled approximately $9.58 million. CoinGlass data also showed Spot Market Netflow of -$9.74 million across ten days.

Negative Spot Market Netflow indicated that more PONS left exchanges than entered them.

Such withdrawals may reduce immediately available selling supply. However, Netflow data alone cannot confirm investors’ holding intentions.

Continued outflows could support a breakout. Still, buyers must defend $0.64 before PONS can realistically challenge $0.97 and $1.

Final Summary

  • PONS gained 13% and approached the critical $0.64 resistance level.
  • Improving MACD suggested stronger momentum, although the negative A/D still favored sellers.

data.title: XRP Ledger’s Batch V1.1 is one vote away – Can 8 transactions change XRPL?
data.description:
One block, eight different transactions – A pass or a miss?

This year, high-performance Layer-1 networks have implemented various upgrades with the primary objective of enhancing “scalability.” XRP Ledger is clearly not an exception, with its proposed “Batch V1.1” solution. The upgrade allows up to eight different transactions in a block in an attempt to increase throughput while allowing the ledger to scale further. 

But will this upgrade actually move the needle for XRP Ledger?

Based on the current validator vote, it seems the market is betting on a yes. Batch V1.1 has already gotten 27 out of 35 validator votes, and only needs one more vote to meet the 80% threshold needed to activate the upgrade.

That said, the upgrade has found some skeptics. 

Batch V1.1 is designed for “dependent” transactions, meaning one transaction relies on the success of another transaction.

If one fails, the entire batch fails. This all-or-nothing setup could cause issues with execution and security, especially after the earlier Batch V1.0 bug.

However, a majority of validator support means that most people using the XRPL are confident that there would be few security concerns.

And while such a conviction alone can be a good sign for XRPL’s future growth, the question of the timing is significant. XRP Ledger posted a strong Q3, putting its on-chain fundamentals in focus as Q4 approaches.

But with Batch V1.1 now just one vote away, could this upgrade give XRPL’s growing on-chain activity another boost in the final quarter?

XRP Ledger heads into Q4 with a key on-chain gap

There is an apparent divergence in Ripple’s [XRP] Q3 cycle.

From a technical perspective, XRP rose over 35%, its first bullish quarter since Q3 2025, but on-chain activity has not kept up with the recovery.

For example, the XRP Ledger recorded $416 million in DEX volume so far in Q3, still below the previous quarter’s $469 million. The same gap is evident for other crucial metrics.

As the chart below demonstrates, XRP Ledger’s transaction count stands at around 162 million, far below the 222 million in the previous quarter, despite XRP closing Q2 with a 22% drop.

In other words, the price of XRP rose substantially in Q3, but the underlying network activity has yet to follow the same trend.

In this respect, the upgrade of Batch V1.1 could not have come at a better time. 

XRP has recorded strong price gains, but on-chain activity is still lagging.

By making dependent transactions easier to process in batches, the upgrade could increase transaction efficiency, thus supporting higher network activity. Therefore, its activation is a “timely” catalyst for the XRP Ledger heading into Q4.

Final Summary

  • One vote away, the upgrade could make XRP Ledger transactions faster and more efficient.
  • XRP rose over 35%, but network activity stayed weaker, making the upgrade important for Q4.

data.title: Top 8 DEXs every crypto trader should know about in September 2026
data.description:
Crypto exchanges give users a way to buy, sell, and swap digital assets, but they do not all operate in the same way. Centralised exchanges (CEXs) act as intermediaries, typically taking custody of users’ funds and matching trades through their own infrastructure. Decentralised exchanges (DEXs), on the other hand, use blockchain-based smart contracts to facilitate trades directly from a user’s wallet. This gives users greater control over their assets and removes the need to rely on a central platform to hold their funds.

DEXs have evolved considerably over the years, with platforms now offering different approaches to liquidity, trading mechanisms, supported networks, and fees. However, trading on a DEX also comes with considerations such as network costs, slippage, liquidity, and smart-contract risk. As a result, choosing a DEX is less about finding one platform that works for everyone and more about finding one that fits a trader’s needs. That said, here are the top 8 DEXs every crypto trader should know about in September 2026.

1. SushiSwap

SushiSwap is a multi-chain DEX that supports 25+ blockchains, giving users access to a wider range of networks than most of the platforms on this list. Its SushiXSwap feature allows users to swap tokens across different chains without having to manage external bridges themselves. The platform also supports standard AMM-based trading and has a native SUSHI token, while network fees depend on the blockchain being used.

SushiSwap has also remained popular among users interested in yield farming through its Onsen program, which provides incentives for supplying liquidity to selected pools. However, spreading liquidity across so many networks can result in more fragmented markets, and its trading volume has generally remained below Uniswap’s in recent years. Even so, its broad chain coverage and cross-chain swaps make it worth considering for traders who regularly move between different blockchain ecosystems.

2. Hyperliquid

Hyperliquid is built on its own Layer-1 blockchain and is mainly known for its perpetual futures trading. Rather than using an automated market maker, it runs a fully on-chain order book, giving traders a setup that feels closer to a centralised exchange while still keeping trades on-chain. It can process up to 200,000 orders per second, and traders do not pay gas when placing or cancelling orders. This combination has made Hyperliquid particularly appealing to users who want faster execution for more active trading strategies.

The platform offers 100+ trading pairs and up to 50x leverage on perpetuals, with liquidity concentrated around its derivatives markets. Users also remain in control of their funds instead of handing custody to a centralised exchange. However, assets need to be bridged to Hyperliquid’s L1, and its spot trading selection is smaller than that of many AMM-based DEXs. For traders primarily interested in perpetuals, though, its order-book model and low-cost trading make it one of the more notable DEXs to consider.

3. dYdX

dYdX is mainly focused on derivatives, offering perpetuals and margin trading through a fully decentralised order book. With its v4 upgrade, the platform moved to its own Cosmos-based app-chain, allowing validators to process trades rather than relying on any external centralised matching system. Traders can use leverage and advanced order types while keeping custody of their funds, making dYdX more suited to users who want a trading setup similar to a traditional exchange but on-chain.

The platform also has its own token, DYDX, which has high trading volumes across its major markets. Its focus on derivatives means it is not designed to be a general-purpose DEX for every type of swap, but it offers more trading tools than many simpler platforms. Users do need to get set up on the dYdX app-chain, and the platform is currently geo-blocked in the US, which limits access for traders in that region.

4. Uniswap

It’s no surprise that Uniswap is on the list, as the DEX has helped popularise the automated market maker (AMM) model used across DeFi. It remains a major source of spot liquidity, particularly for Ethereum-based tokens, and allows users to swap assets without going through a centralised intermediary. The platform is available across several networks, including Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, and BNB Chain, giving traders more options depending on the assets they want to trade and the network fees they are willing to pay.

The launch of Uniswap v4 also introduced hooks, which allow developers to customise how liquidity pools operate and add new functionality around trades. Ethereum mainnet transactions can still be expensive when network activity is high, but using Uniswap on Layer-2 networks such as Arbitrum and Optimism can reduce those costs. Its deep liquidity and permissionless listing model make it particularly useful for traders looking for a wide range of spot assets, although liquidity providers still need to account for risks such as impermanent loss.

5. 1inch

1inch is a DEX aggregator rather than an exchange itself, bringing liquidity from multiple decentralised platforms into one place. It searches across multiple decentralised exchanges like Uniswap, SushiSwap, and Curve to find a suitable route for each trade, which can help users get a better price or reduce slippage than they might find by checking a single DEX. The platform supports 10+ networks, including Ethereum, BNB Chain, and Polygon, and its Fusion mode also allows users to make swaps without paying gas directly.

The routing can also help protect trades from MEV and front-running, although more complicated routes may use more gas, particularly for smaller transactions. With liquidity pulled from hundreds of sources, 1inch can be useful for traders who want to compare execution across the wider DeFi market without manually checking several exchanges. The amount of information shown on the platform can take some getting used to, especially for those who are new to DEX aggregators.

6. ApeSwap

ApeSwap is a community-driven DEX focused on staking, yield farming, and liquidity mining, with support for networks including BNB Chain, Polygon, Ethereum, and Telos. Its most distinctive feature is its Treasury Bills, which allow users to buy certain tokens at a discount. Alongside its standard AMM-based trading and farming features, this gives ApeSwap a stronger focus on earning yield rather than simply swapping assets.

The platform uses BANANA as its native token and generally has relatively low network costs, although its liquidity and trading volumes are lower than those of the larger DEXs. ApeSwap also has a strong community presence, but users should pay attention to the risks that come with yield products, including the potential impact of high inflation in reward tokens. For users specifically looking for staking and farming opportunities, however, it offers more options than a straightforward token-swapping platform.

7. Swapzone

Swapzone is a non-custodial crypto services aggregator that lets users compare several exchange providers before completing a swap. It brings together information such as real-time exchange rates, estimated processing times, supported assets, and KYC requirements, so users can check their options before committing to a provider. This can be especially useful for those who want to avoid unexpected verification requirements or simply find a rate and processing time that suit them.

Swapzone also includes provider ratings and verified community reviews, giving users more information to consider alongside the advertised rates. The actual exchange is completed through the provider selected by the user, so features and KYC policies can vary between services. While comparing several providers may take a little longer, the platform gives users a clearer picture of their options before making a swap.

8. Curve Finance

Curve Finance is particularly useful for swapping assets that are designed to hold a similar value, such as USDC and USDT or ETH and stETH. Its specialised bonding curve is designed to keep slippage low on these trades, which makes Curve a popular choice for larger swaps where even small differences in execution can matter. The DEX is available across networks including Ethereum, Avalanche, Fantom, Polygon, Arbitrum and Optimism, while its CRV token is used within the Curve ecosystem.

Curve is also closely tied to DeFi’s yield farming sector, with users able to provide liquidity to its pools and earn returns from their deposited assets. Its stablecoin pools have made it an important part of the wider DeFi market, although the platform is less suited to trading highly volatile assets. New users may also find its interface less straightforward than some newer DEXs.

Final thoughts 

DEXs have become an important part of the crypto market by giving traders a way to swap and trade assets directly from their wallets without relying on a centralised intermediary. As the sector has developed, different platforms have focused on areas such as spot trading, derivatives, cross-chain swaps, liquidity provision and yield farming, giving traders more options depending on what they need. However, factors such as liquidity, fees, slippage, supported networks and smart-contract risks can vary significantly between platforms. Users should do their own research, understand how a DEX works, and test the platform with smaller amounts before committing significant capital.

data.title: XRP gets 26% share in Grayscale’s ‘next gen’ portfolio – No space for Bitcoin
data.description:
Grayscale has come up with ready-made crypto investment portfolios that financial advisors can use for their clients, but there is something unusual. The investment giant launched four different model portfolios, each with a different purpose.

In this, the “Digital Assets Core Plus portfolio” is designed as a broad, foundational crypto allocation and includes Bitcoin [BTC], Ethereum [ETH], Solana [SOL], and Chainlink [LINK].

Meanwhile, ‘Digital Assets Leaders’ focuses on the five largest eligible crypto assets available through Grayscale’s single-asset products. Whereas “Digital Assets Next Gen” is designed to give investors exposure to crypto assets beyond Bitcoin, including both established and emerging projects.

Finally, “Digital Assets Infrastructure” focuses on assets tied to protocols that support areas such as smart contracts and tokenization. 

Grayscale gives more weightage to XRP than Bitcoin

Now the catch here is that Ripple’s XRP has received a huge allocation in the Digital Assets Next Gen portfolio. As of the 31st of August, the portfolio had seven holdings, with Ethereum at 42.34%, XRP at 26.11%, and Solana at 21.09%.

Bitcoin, however, has been left out of this portfolio. Together, those three assets account for roughly 90% of the portfolio. Meanwhile, the remaining allocation is spread across Hyperliquid [HYPE], LINK, Avalanche [AVAX], and Sui [SUI].

Interestingly, Grayscale has also capped each asset to not go beyond 40% in a model. However, the portfolios are subject to rebalancing every quarter, wherein Grayscale can change the allocations as market capitalization and the eligible asset universe change.

This comes after Grayscale filed an amendment that could move its Litecoin Trust closer to an ETF structure. 

Is altcoin season incoming? 

Meanwhile, on the price front, XRP was trading at $1.40 at the time of reporting after a hike of almost 40% in the past month. Compared to this altcoin, Bitcoin was changing hands at $76,846.10 at press time after a hike of 22.1% in the past month. 

Whereas its Bitcoin dominance was testing resistance at 59.27%. This means Bitcoin’s share of the total crypto market was approaching a level where it has historically struggled to move higher.

So, now if dominance breaks above this level, Bitcoin could continue outperforming altcoins, while a rejection could signal capital rotating toward altcoins such as XRP, Solana, and Ethereum.

But with the altcoin season index sitting at 36 at press time, it is confirmed that Bitcoin is here to rule for now.

Final Summary

  • Ripple’s XRP has received a huge allocation in the Digital Assets Next Gen portfolio.
  • Bitcoin, on the other hand, has been excluded from the portfolio.

data.title: CAP crypto jumps 38%, yet bulls should be cautious – Here’s why
data.description:
Cap [CAP], the native token for the blockchain credit-backed platform, has pulled impressive numbers over the past day. At press time, its market capitalization crossed over $100 million, while its price traded at $0.06 following a 38% increase within this period.

AMBCrypto observed that much of this growth can be attributed to a sentiment-driven rally in the market. Notably, Mindshare and sentiment for the asset have both increased significantly over the last day.

The Sentiment, most particularly, which is an indicator that tracks the extent of the bullish or bearish outlook investors hold using a scale between -10 and 10, has a reading of 4.27, suggesting that the market is bullish at the time being.

Likewise, there has been noticeable growth in the Mindshare, which represents the amount of discussion among traders about the asset. CoinMarketCap put the number at over 679% to 984 in the past 24 hours alone.

Growth in the Sentiment alongside Mindshare often impacts price positively, in a way that contributes to the overall interest among investors holding the asset in the near term.

On-chain capital flow is not a strong bull case

The contribution to the rally through on-chain flow has remained largely minimal, according to data from DeFiLlama.

In the past 48 hours, the Total Value Locked, which tracks the amount of the asset deposited into the protocol, had grown slightly by $10 million, bringing its value to about $330 million at the time of writing.

While the growth is moderate and tells that investors are bullish, it is not quite at a level that is often associated with a rally that trends across multiple trading sessions in the market.

The fees and Active Loans, although positive, have remained minimal. The total fees generated by the protocol in the past 24 hours reached just $11,758, while the Active Loans stood at $61.55 million at press time.

The Active Loans, for instance, represent a slight decline from the $67.86 million recorded on the 12th of September, while the Fees generated show a massive gap from the $44,130 recorded on the same day. The clear decline often suggests fewer active users of

the protocol, a trend that ultimately impacts the asset’s utility eventually.

The risk of a decline remains

The risk of a decline persists as the flow of capital across the spot and perpetual markets has shown weakness.

Data from CoinGlass shows that the OI-Weighted Funding Rate for CAP had plummeted into negative territory and has a reading of about -0.4748%.

A negative Funding Rate implies that traders are concentrating more of their capital into shorting the asset, meaning they anticipate that the asset is likely to trade lower on the chart in the near term.

In the same vein, there has been a heightened sell-off in the spot market at the same time, with the Spot Market Netflow dropping to around $2.20 million in the past 24 hours in the market, following $9.78 million.

Continued selling in the market would continue to weigh on the price, causing it to underperform in the near term. For now, the risk of a decline is still on the high side, especially when the Sentiment fades.

Final Summary

  • CAP gained 38% as its Market Capitalization crossed $100 million, while Sentiment and Mindshare rose sharply.

  • Weak on-chain flows, falling Spot Market Netflow, and a negative Funding Rate keep the risk of a decline elevated.

data.title: $350M in Ethereum exits exchanges as Q4 battle with Bitcoin begins
data.description:
The market has preferred Ethereum over Bitcoin in Q3, but the trend could face a test in Q4.

Technically speaking, the ETH/BTC ratio is set to finish the quarter more than 19% higher, the first ETH-driven outperformance since the third quarter of 2025. But the real question is whether Ethereum will be able to maintain its lead as the market enters the fourth quarter.

According to CoinGlass, the fourth quarter has traditionally been Bitcoin’s strongest quarter, with average gains of more than 77%. Ethereum, in comparison, has delivered an average Q4 ROI of around 18%.

This seasonal disparity could become a major headwind for ETH/BTC, especially after Ethereum’s strong Q3 rally.

More importantly, the historical data shows another key pattern. 

Bitcoin has outperformed Ethereum in 8 out of the last 9 Q4 cycles, with 2021 being the only exception. Besides, BTC has typically posted lower losses in bear markets.

This dynamic suggests that Bitcoin is consistently resilient in both bullish and bearish environments, gaining more ground during risk-on periods and posting lower losses during risk-off ones. 

According to AMBCrypto, this scenario is even more relevant in the current macro setup. Q4 is expected to start with elevated volatility. If the risk appetite decreases, then Bitcoin’s historical pattern could give it an edge over Ethereum.

Ethereum supply shock builds ahead of Q4

Ethereum is entering Q4 with rising odds of breaking the historical performance pattern.

Ethereum’s supply setup is getting increasingly tight. According to Santiment data, only 6.06 million ETH is currently on exchanges, down from 22.9 million at the June 2020 peak.

This trend is accelerating, with around 140,000 ETH worth of around $350 million now leaving exchanges over the past 96 hours.

In addition, the staking ratio for Ethereum has reached a new all-time high, while Bitmine added 27,180 ETH last week. However, a larger indication of this is the developing divergence between ETH and BTC exchange supply.

As the chart below shows, only 12.7% of ETH supply is currently held on exchanges, compared with 16.5% for BTC, a nearly four-percentage-point difference.

This divergence shows a clear shift in investor positioning. 

In a risk-off environment, that matters because lower exchange balances imply less ETH available for selling. So, even if volatility picks up in Q4, Ethereum could experience less sell-side pressure, providing it with a better setup for a rebound when demand returns. 

In this regard, Ethereum’s [ETH] tightening supply could challenge its historical Q4 weakness. With renewed demand, lower exchange balances could give ETH a much-needed boost towards breaking its usual Q4 pattern against Bitcoin and becoming a better macro hedge.

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin has historically performed better than Ethereum in Q4.
  • Tighter ETH supply could help Ethereum rebound if demand returns.

data.title: Top 6 crypto exchanges to trade on in September 2026
data.description:
Crypto exchanges are online platforms that let traders buy, sell, and exchange cryptocurrencies and tokens. Centralized and decentralized exchanges are the two major types of exchanges that users can trade on. Centralized exchanges act like marketplaces where the trades are managed by an intermediary, which is a central authority.

Decentralized exchanges do not have an intermediary that manages the custody of assets and trades and operate entirely on a blockchain. They have a peer-to-peer network that uses blockchain technology and smart contracts to govern and manage all the transactions.

Here are the top 6 crypto exchanges of September 2026:

1. Coinbase

Coinbase has built its reputation around having a simple user interface and straightforward fiat on-ramps. It was founded in 2012 and started out as a simple Bitcoin buying platform; it is still regarded as one of the most compliant and institution-friendly exchanges in the world.

The platform intends to increase economic freedom in the world and stores more digital assets than any other company. It is creating a one-stop solution for users who want to access equities, crypto, derivatives, and prediction markets. It also offers an advanced trading service that gives traders a chance to access real-time order books with 0% maker fees.

2. Binance 

Binance is one of the most popular crypto exchanges in the world and offers a suite of products, including the largest digital asset exchange. The platform works with the mission that everyone should have the freedom to earn, hold, and share their money.

The platform has a suite of products such as the exchange, Binance Labs, Binance Academy, Binance Research, and much more. Users are at the heart of Binance, and user protection lies at the core of the platform; they have state-of-the-art security measures and stringent data privacy controls.

3. OKX

OKX was founded in 2013 and functions as a centralized exchange that offers spot, margin, options, staking, and perpetual futures. Users can take control of their financial future and trade over 300 cryptocurrencies with low fees.

The platform has over 70M users around the world, and all assets are backed 1:1 and publicly verifiable through our Proof of Reserves, giving users full visibility into how their funds are secured.

4. Paradex

Paradex is a decentralized exchange that focuses on delivering derivatives trading with the speed and liquidity associated with centralised platforms. The architecture mixes an off-chain order book with on-chain settlement, letting trades execute quickly while also maintaining privacy through encrypted account data.

Paradex supports more than 250 trading pairs, and the leverage goes up to 50X on major assets such as Bitcoin and Ethereum. The platform’s fee structure is a key distinguishing feature, and it lets retail traders access zero-fee perpetual trading while the options markets follow a different maker-taker model.

5. Crypto.com

Crypto.com is an exchange with over 150 million users across 90 countries. It lets users buy, sell, trade, and manage digital assets and is designed for both beginner and experienced traders. The platform’s ecosystem has an exchange, mobile app, digital wallet, and payment solution.

There are 400+ cryptocurrencies available to trade and up to 100X leverage on perpetuals and futures. Crypto.com is known for its accessibility and requires a minimum deposit of just $1 to get started, along with maker fees of 0.08% to 0.25% and taker fees of 0.18% to 0.50% depending on the 30-day trading volume.

6. Gate.io 

Gate.io was founded in 2013 and provides safe, reliable, transparent, and authentic digital asset trading services. It supports over 5200+ digital assets and 12,800 stocks, giving users one-stop access to trading.

It is also one of the first exchanges in the world to commit to 100% Proof of Reserves. It also ranks among the top 3 in the world in spot volume, liquidity, and futures volume. It also has its own blockchain ecosystem called the GateChain.

Final word

The cryptocurrency space has come a long way over the years, with platforms offering a wide range of tools, services, and features that are designed to suit various trading styles and investment goals.

The choice that any user makes will depend on their requirements and should be based on their own research.

data.title: Dogecoin whales accumulate 240M DOGE – Why is price still falling?
data.description:
Dogecoin [DOGE] has been in a retracement over the past three weeks, and the price correction appears not to be ending soon. This trend is happening as the broader memecoin market follows suit.

In fact, the top ten memecoins by market cap are all in the red over the past 24 hours. As spot whales take advantage of the correction, can it help turn around the short-term price direction?

Spot whale accumulation intensifies as price corrects

Whales continue to accumulate the memecoin at discounted prices. That is, the number of DOGE held by whales rose from 18.72 billion to around 19 billion tokens over the past week.

A crypto analyst noted that spot holders bought over 240 million DOGE tokens worth over $20 million. However, this buying activity does not guarantee consequential price appreciation.

Instead, the activity suggests confidence may be building ahead of the next potential rebound. This activity explains the current price action outlook of the memecoin.

Can DOGE’s 0.618 Fib level hold?

On the charts, Dogecoin was trading around the 0.618 Fibonacci retracement level after its strong trend from $0.07 to $0.10. Currently, bulls are facing resistance at $0.085, aligning with the 50% retracement level.

The lower support band of the 4-hour sideways range is at $0.082, which is the most recent demand area that pushed the price to $0.095. Hence, holding above $0.080 and breaking past $0.085 would expose $0.10 again.

But the market structure is mildly bearish, and losing $0.080 as support would reinforce this view. This projection is because the Bull Bear Power (BBP) was red at press time, while the RSI at 40 is 10 points away from the oversold territory.

This indicates that selling pressure is yet to be exhausted. Who were these sellers then?

Why is the price falling?

As per CryptoQuant data, big whales have dominated the Futures Average Order Size since DOGE hit $0.10 on the 22nd of August. This was a hint of profit-taking as large holder activity surged after a rally. Further analysis of the Futures Taker CVD confirmed that sellers were the dominant force.

Source: CryptoQuantAdditionally, the change in Open Interest (OI) was down across major exchanges like Binance, OKX, Bybit, KuCoin, and Gate. For instance, DOGE’s OI fell by 5% on the KuCoin Futures market, as per CoinGlass data.

Therefore, Dogecoin’s price is falling despite whale accumulation due to profit-taking of leveraged orders, OI decline, and derivative selling.

Final Summary

  • Dogecoin whales accumulated over 240 million DOGE in the past week amid the recent price correction. 
  • DOGE was trading at the 0.618 Fibonacci level, which is a key bounce zone, but sellers were yet to be exhausted.
